---
title: "Bayesian Prop Hazard w/ Frailty: Weibull"
output: pdf_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(rstan)
library(survival)
library(tidyverse)
options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())
```

## Data

```{r}
## Importing it
kidney_data <- kidney

## Covariates defined to match the paper: age in years, sex coded 1 = male, 2 = female,
## 0/1 indicators for disease types GN, AN, PKD ("Other" is the baseline).
X <- cbind(age = kidney_data$age,
           sex = kidney_data$sex,
           GN  = as.integer(k$disease == "GN"),
           AN  = as.integer(k$disease == "AN"),
           PKD = as.integer(k$disease == "PKD"))

## List format to align with the stan model
stan_data <- list(N = length(kidney_data$id),
                  M = length(unique(kidney_data$id)),
                  P = ncol(X),
                  t = k$time,
                  C = k$status,
                  id = k$id,
                  X = X)
```

## Fit

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results="hide"}
fit <- stan(file = "Weibull_v1.stan",
            data = stan_data,
            seed = 1,
            chains = 4,
            iter = 2000,
            refresh = 0)
```

## Results

```{r}
print(fit, pars = c("beta", "sigma2"), probs = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))
```

Paper values for comparison (McGilchrist & Aisbett 1991, Table 2): age 0.0063, sex -1.7947, GN 0.2062, AN 0.4099, PKD -1.2961, sigma^2 0.3821. Missing by some margin for a number of our estimates. 

```{r}
print(fit, pars = "Z", probs = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))
```

Paper values are 2.3, 1.9, 1.2, 0.5, 1.5, etc... There are some improvements needed to this model and therefore I'm not formalising the comparisons yet.

## Diagnostics

```{r diagnostics}
traceplot(fit, pars = c("beta", "sigma"))
rstan::get_num_divergent(fit)
```
